title: More than three million people flee Ukraine in three weeks
body:
By 15 March 2022, the twentieth day of Russia's invasion, about 3 million people had fled Ukraine, according to the International Organization for Migration. More than 150,000 of them were third-country nationals. Millions more remained inside Ukraine, either at home or as internally displaced people. Ukrainian men were barred from leaving the country and urged to fight, so many of the refugees were women and children.

Most refugees went to Poland, where the border force reported 1.83 million arrivals of Ukrainian refugees. Data cited by the UN refugee agency, UNHCR, also showed 453,432 in Romania, 337,215 in Moldova, 263,888 in Hungary and 213,000 in Slovakia. Russia reported 142,994 arrivals according to Moscow's data, and Belarus received a relatively small number.

Czech authorities estimated, based on mobile phone data, that between 200,000 and 270,000 Ukrainian refugees were in the Czech Republic, and more than 160,000 had been granted residence permits. Russian forces had encircled some Ukrainian cities, including Mariupol, where evacuation attempts had failed, so many civilians could not leave.
